key_insight: High-resolution power traces from generative AI workloads can be systematically scaled and integrated with facility-level telemetry to produce accurate whole‑facility power profiles for data center infrastructure planning.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between proprietary, variable-resolution workload power data and the needs of whole‑facility energy and capacity planning, enabling repeatable, transparent estimates of data center power demand driven by generative AI.
method: Collect high-resolution workload power telemetry (GPU/host) during representative generative AI tasks and isolate duty-cycle and transient behavior.
Develop mapping/scaling rules and validation procedures to translate workload-level measurements into facility-level power contributions (including PUE and cooling impacts).
Apply the methodology to diverse workload mixes to generate whole‑facility profiles, identify peak drivers, and quantify planning margins.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners, operators, and planners with actionable, reproducible power profiles so they can size power/cooling infrastructure, anticipate peak loads, optimize deployment, and make more informed cost and sustainability decisions.
visual_elements: Time-series chart of high-resolution workload power (GPU, CPU, host) showing duty cycles and transients
Stacked facility power breakdown (compute + cooling + networking + overhead) derived from workload scaling
Flow diagram showing measurement-to-facility mapping pipeline (telemetry → scaling rules → validation → whole‑facility profile)
Heatmap or histogram of peak frequency and duration to highlight planning-relevant extremes
paper_title: Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning
paper_authors: Roberto Vercellino, Jared Willard, Gustavo Campos, Weslley da Silva Pereira, Olivia Hull
